variants.title: Protect the branch
variants.context: A protected branch advances only after policy is revalidated for the exact candidate commit and the expected target head. Search, Actions, notifications, audit, and webhooks consume the committed result; none becomes the source of truth for history.
variants.prompt: Two merges race for the same target branch. What prevents a lost update?
options: Atomically advance the reference only if its old value still matches the expected head; the loser retries policy evaluation.
A global lock on all repositories.
optionFeedback: Compare-and-swap on the reference is the safety mechanism.
A global lock is unnecessary and slow.
variants.hint: What must be true of the target head at commit time?
variants.explanation: Policy is revalidated for the exact candidate and target head.

variants.title: Protect the branch
variants.context: A protected branch advances only after policy is revalidated for the exact candidate commit and the expected target head. Search, Actions, notifications, audit, and webhooks consume the committed result; none becomes the source of truth for history.
variants.prompt: The search index is behind. Is repository history wrong?
options: No. Search is a derived view; the protected reference is the truth and search catches up.
optionFeedback: Derived systems consume the committed result.
History lives in the repository service.
Lag is a freshness matter, not correctness.
variants.explanation: None of the derived systems may become the source of truth.

variants.title: Protect the branch
variants.context: A protected branch advances only after policy is revalidated for the exact candidate commit and the expected target head. Search, Actions, notifications, audit, and webhooks consume the committed result; none becomes the source of truth for history.
variants.prompt: A webhook subscriber is down for an hour. May merges continue?
options: Yes. Writes stay durable; events queue with bounded retries per subscriber.
optionFeedback: Subscriber failure must not become a repository outage.
Blocking developers for a webhook is backwards.
variants.hint: Which path is synchronous, and which is not?
variants.explanation: The synchronous path ends after the authorized durable update.

variants.title: Budget the fan-out
variants.context: Planning envelope: 18K repository events per second, 12 downstream subscribers per event, and 30% delivery headroom. Backlog is a freshness budget: measure the age of the oldest undelivered event per consumer.
variants.prompt: 18,000 events per second with 12 subscribers each. How many deliveries per second?
variants.explanation: 18,000 × 12 = 216,000 delivery attempts per second before retries.

mistakes.feedback: Each event fans out to twelve subscribers.

variants.title: Budget the fan-out
variants.context: Planning envelope: 18K repository events per second, 12 downstream subscribers per event, and 30% delivery headroom. Backlog is a freshness budget: measure the age of the oldest undelivered event per consumer.
variants.prompt: 216,000 deliveries per second with 2 KB payloads. How many MB per second of event egress?
variants.explanation: 216,000 × 2 KB = 432,000 KB/s = 432 MB/s; keep large blobs out of envelopes.

variants.title: Budget the fan-out
variants.context: Planning envelope: 18K repository events per second, 12 downstream subscribers per event, and 30% delivery headroom. Backlog is a freshness budget: measure the age of the oldest undelivered event per consumer.
variants.prompt: Adding one more subscriber to every event adds how many deliveries per second at 18,000 events per second?
variants.explanation: 18,000 more deliveries per second; adding a consumer can cost more than a modest write increase.

mistakes.feedback: That is the existing total, not the increase.

variants.title: Trace the merge
variants.context: The merge path: load the candidate SHA, target head, permissions, reviews, checks, and policy; verify objects and atomically advance the reference only if its old value still matches, recording the transition; publish a versioned event from the journal; derived consumers update with separate offsets and retries.
variants.prompt: A pull request is merged. Put the path in order.

items.text: Load the candidate SHA, current target head, permissions, reviews, required checks, and branch policy; reject evidence for other commits.
Verify objects exist, atomically advance the target reference only if its old value still matches, and record the transition durably.
Publish a versioned event with repository, actor, old and new references, policy version, and trace ID from the journal.
Update search, notifications, Actions, audit, analytics, and webhook queues with separate offsets and retries.

variants.hint: Publication follows the durable reference change.
variants.explanation: The protected reference commits once; replayable consumers derive their views.

variants.title: Trace the merge
variants.context: The merge path: load the candidate SHA, target head, permissions, reviews, checks, and policy; verify objects and atomically advance the reference only if its old value still matches, recording the transition; publish a versioned event from the journal; derived consumers update with separate offsets and retries.
variants.prompt: The target head moved after evaluation. Put the path in order.

items.text: Evidence was loaded for the candidate against the old target head.
The compare-and-swap fails because the reference’s value changed.
The coordinator re-evaluates mergeability and policy against the new head.
On success, the transition is recorded and the event published.

variants.hint: A stale evaluation must not advance the branch.
variants.explanation: Compare-and-swap retries are the merge coordinator’s job.

variants.title: Trace the merge
variants.context: The merge path: load the candidate SHA, target head, permissions, reviews, checks, and policy; verify objects and atomically advance the reference only if its old value still matches, recording the transition; publish a versioned event from the journal; derived consumers update with separate offsets and retries.
variants.prompt: A required check passed on an older commit of the PR. Put the path in order.

items.text: The coordinator loads status evidence bound to exact commit SHAs.
The evidence belongs to a different commit than the candidate: rejected.
No event is published; the author is told which check is missing for the current commit.

variants.hint: Evidence is bound to commits, not to the pull request.
variants.explanation: Reject evidence that belongs to a different commit.

variants.title: Bind the evidence
variants.context: Bind review and status evidence to exact commit identities, not mutable pull-request labels. Mutable handles must resolve to immutable commits and a target-head version.
variants.prompt: An approval was given on commit A; the author pushed commit B. Is the approval valid for B?
options: No. Review evidence binds to the reviewed commit; B needs its own evidence unless policy says otherwise.
optionFeedback: Mutable PR labels cannot carry commit-bound evidence.
variants.hint: Which commit did the reviewer look at?
variants.explanation: Bind evidence to exact commit identities.

variants.title: Bind the evidence
variants.context: Bind review and status evidence to exact commit identities, not mutable pull-request labels. Mutable handles must resolve to immutable commits and a target-head version.
variants.prompt: Which fields must a status record carry?
options: Check name, exact commit SHA, conclusion, attempt, producer identity, completion time, and artifact link.
optionFeedback: A bare result cannot be bound.
variants.hint: What makes the evidence verifiable later?
variants.explanation: Status evidence names the exact commit.

variants.title: Bind the evidence
variants.context: Bind review and status evidence to exact commit identities, not mutable pull-request labels. Mutable handles must resolve to immutable commits and a target-head version.
variants.prompt: Why keep a monotonically increasing version on a protected reference?
options: So decisions record which target-head version they used and stale evaluations are detectable.
optionFeedback: Versioning makes compare-and-swap and audit precise.
variants.hint: How do you know an evaluation is stale?
variants.explanation: Record the target-head version each decision used.

variants.title: Isolate the fleet
variants.context: Repository writes stay durable when a derived consumer is slow; one repository or subscriber cannot exhaust the shared fleet; webhook retries are bounded per subscriber with dead-letter handling.
variants.prompt: A single hot repository generates most events. What protects other repositories’ delivery?
options: Partitioning, per-repository and per-subscriber bounds, and separate backlog measurement.
optionFeedback: Bound one repository or subscriber from exhausting the shared fleet.
Shared queues without bounds are the failure.
variants.hint: What does one hot tenant do to a shared queue?
variants.explanation: Load-test with a hot repository, a slow subscriber, a retry burst, and a failed zone.

variants.title: Isolate the fleet
variants.context: Repository writes stay durable when a derived consumer is slow; one repository or subscriber cannot exhaust the shared fleet; webhook retries are bounded per subscriber with dead-letter handling.
variants.prompt: Which backlog metric maps to the developer-visible promise?
options: The age of the oldest undelivered event per consumer.

variants.title: Isolate the fleet
variants.context: Repository writes stay durable when a derived consumer is slow; one repository or subscriber cannot exhaust the shared fleet; webhook retries are bounded per subscriber with dead-letter handling.
variants.prompt: A customer webhook endpoint fails continuously. What should the webhook service do?
options: Retry with bounds per subscriber, dead-letter, and expose replay controls.
Drop all events for that customer silently.
optionFeedback: Bounded retries plus dead-letter handling isolate the failure.
variants.hint: How long should one subscriber consume delivery capacity?
variants.explanation: The webhook service owns bounded retries and dead-letter handling.
